sections.h2: Who records deeds in Sanilac County, Michigan?
sections.html:
The Sanilac County Register of Deeds, based in the county seat of Sandusky, is the official recording office for every document that affects real property in the county. Its list of services covers warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, mortgages, mortgage assignments and discharges, land contracts, liens, easements, plats, surveys and court orders that touch land.

The office does not draft documents or answer legal questions, so a seller who needs a deed prepared should go to an attorney or a title company first. Questions about a document that has already been drafted can go to the office at the county Register of Deeds page or by phone at (810) 648-2313.

The county also posts a weekly list of land transfers, so you can see which parcels changed hands in each township during a given week. Sanilac is the largest county in Michigan's Lower Peninsula by land area, at about 963 square miles of land, which means a deed can describe a farm parcel in the Thumb as easily as a lakeshore cottage near Lexington.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Sanilac County?
sections.html:
Recording a deed in Sanilac County costs $30 per document no matter how many pages it has, and the transfer taxes add $8.60 for every $1,000 of the sale price. The county's fee schedule lists each charge, and the table below pulls them together.

Sanilac County Register of Deeds charges for a typical sale
ChargeAmountSource
Recording a deed or mortgage$30 per documentMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3MCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Tax certificate from the county treasurer$5County fee schedule
County transfer tax$1.10 per $1,000MCL 207.504
State transfer tax$7.50 per $1,000MCL 207.525
Copy of a real estate record$1 per page, $5 to certifyCounty fee schedule

For a $160,000 sale, the two transfer taxes come to $1,376 (160 units of $1,000 at $8.60). Add the $30 recording fee and the $5 tax certificate and the government charges on the deed total $1,411.

sections.h2: Who pays the transfer tax on a Sanilac County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays. Michigan's state transfer tax act makes the seller or grantor liable, and it requires payment to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered, although in practice the Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is recorded.

The deed must state the full value of the real property on its face, or an affidavit of value must be attached. When a sale includes both land and personal property, the tax applies only to the real estate if the two values are stated separately.

Several transfers are exempt. Under the state act these include:

  • A deed given for less than $100 in consideration.
  • A conveyance from a parent to a child, stepchild or adopted child, and from a grandparent to a grandchild.
  • A court judgment or order that transfers land without a stated price.
  • A deed given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure of a government-backed loan.
  • A land contract, until legal title passes to the buyer.

The county act has a shorter exemption list and does not include the family transfers, so a parent-to-child deed can owe the county portion while escaping the state portion. Cite the exemption statute on the deed itself, since the office rejects deeds that give neither a price nor an exemption.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like to be accepted for recording?
sections.html:
A deed must meet the formatting rules in Michigan's recording requirements act, MCL 565.201, or the register cannot accept it. The county posts the full text of that statute on its real estate information page.

  • Every signer's name is printed or typed beneath the signature, in black or dark blue ink, and matches the name in the notary acknowledgment.
  • The notary's name is printed near the notary's signature.
  • The grantee's address appears on the deed, and the drafter's name and business address appear too.
  • Pages are 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches, in 10-point type or larger, on white paper of at least 20-pound weight.
  • The first page has a 2.5 inch blank margin at the top and half an inch on the other sides, and its first line states the type of recordable event.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number are removed, and any non-English text comes with an English translation.

A deed that passes these checks cannot be rejected over its content. One that fails any of them comes back unrecorded, which delays the closing.

sections.h2: Does a Sanilac County deed need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
Yes, for warranty deeds. The county treasurer must certify the taxes before the Register of Deeds records any warranty deed, land contract, assignment of a land contract or deed that carries a covenant of warranty, and the treasurer's fee is $5.

A quit claim deed does not carry that requirement on the county's fee schedule, which is one reason family transfers and estate clean-ups often use it. A quit claim conveys whatever interest the grantor holds without a warranty of title, so a buyer paying market price will usually expect a warranty deed backed by title insurance.

Sanilac County has about 21,972 housing units, and the Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied home value of $168,300 for 2020 to 2024. At that median, state and county transfer taxes come to roughly $1,450, which is the figure to keep in mind when you compare net proceeds from different offers.

sections.h2: How do I pay and where do I find recorded documents?
sections.html:
The office takes cash, checks, money orders and credit or debit cards, and checks are made payable to the Sanilac County Register of Deeds. A card payment in person needs a valid photo ID, and the county also runs an online payment location for register of deeds fees through its AllPaid portal.

For research, the county land records site at rod.sanilaccounty.net lets guests search the index for free. Its index reaches back to 1801. Guests can buy PDF copies by card at $1 per page plus a $5 transaction fee per order.

The office also offers a free property fraud alert service. Anyone who owns Sanilac County parcels can subscribe, and the office sends a notice to the owner whenever a document is recorded against a subscribed parcel. That helps catch a forged deed on rural or seasonal property that nobody visits every week.

sections.h2: What is Sanilac County like for sellers?
sections.html:
Sanilac County sits in the Thumb region along Lake Huron, with Huron County to the north, Tuscola and Lapeer to the west and south-west, and St. Clair County to the south. The county was organized in 1849 and had 40,611 residents in the 2020 census; the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 40,083.

Sandusky, Croswell, Marlette and Brown City are the cities, and tourism concentrates in Lexington, Port Sanilac and Carsonville. M-19, M-25, M-46, M-53, M-81 and M-90 carry traffic across the county, and the soil is rich and mostly flat, which keeps farmland a large part of the property mix.

  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 82.6 percent.
  • Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $1,226.
  • Median gross rent: $807.
  • Median household income: $58,863.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 74.

Most buyers here are locals or lakeshore second-home shoppers, so a house inland from the M-25 shoreline often draws a different buyer pool than a cottage at the water.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee for a deed in Sanilac County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30 per document, regardless of page count, under MCL 600.2567. A document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3 for each extra instrument.

faqs.q: What is the combined Michigan transfer tax rate in Sanilac County?
faqs.a: It is $8.60 per $1,000 of value, made up of $7.50 state tax and $1.10 county tax. On a $200,000 sale that is $1,720, and the seller owes it.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed by mail in Sanilac County?
faqs.a: Call the Register of Deeds at (810) 648-2313 before mailing anything. The office confirms the total of recording fee, transfer tax and any tax certificate, and a deed that does not meet MCL 565.201 will be returned unrecorded.

faqs.q: Is a warranty deed treasurer-certified before recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The county treasurer must certify taxes on warranty deeds and land contracts first, and the certificate costs $5. Bring the certified deed to the Register of Deeds for recording.

faqs.q: Does a parent-to-child deed owe transfer tax?
faqs.a: The state tax does not apply to a conveyance from a parent to a child, stepchild or adopted child, or from a grandparent to a grandchild. The county tax act has no such exemption, so ask the office what applies to your deed before you record.
